title: Mon 9 Nov: Nifty reclaims 25,000 on record foreign buying
description:
Hot topic: the Nifty reclaimed 25,000 with a seventh straight gain on a record week of foreign buying, ahead of the first full session of Samvat 2083. Then: banks, Tata Steel, Hindalco, the rupee, oil, US jobs, IT, Titan and M&M.

1. Nifty reclaims 25,000 with a seventh straight gain as banks lead and India shrugs off the US chip rout (5paisa; INDIA IPO (Mint))
2. Nifty Bank jumps 2.3% to 59,086 as ICICI Bank and HDFC Bank lead for a second day (5paisa; Kotak Neo)
3. Tata Steel's September-quarter profit rises 18.2% to 3,666 crore rupees; Nuvama upgrades the stock (Business Today)
4. Hindalco's profit jumps 59% to 7,532 crore rupees as revenue rises 39% (Business Today)
5. Rupee rallies 52 paise to 93.89, its best day in weeks, as the equity surge draws dollars (Telangana Today (PTI); Tapetide; Cappnotes)
6. Brent holds near 98 dollars as Gulf tanker attacks keep a floor under oil (Reuters via Global Banking & Finance)
7. US payrolls beat at 165,000 as the 10-year yield rises to 4.86% (Cappnotes; The Closing Print)
8. Indian IT lags the rally as Nifty IT rises only 0.4% while money moves into banks (5paisa; INDIA IPO (Mint); Cappnotes)
9. Titan hits 5,000 rupees on Dhanteras, up about 10% in three sessions after its results (5paisa; INDIA IPO)
10. M&M extends its post-results rally, rising another 5% to 3,287 rupees (5paisa; INDIA IPO (Mint))

From the Ripple news desk. Voices are AI-generated with open-source Kokoro voices. This is news, not investment advice; the hosts are not SEBI-registered advisers.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Good morning, this is Ripple Daily. I'm P.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: And I'm S. Ten stories, under ten minutes.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Today's big one: the Nifty is back above 25,000, on a record week of foreign buying.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: And today is the first full session of Samvat 2083.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: S, what happened on Friday?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The Nifty rose 2.01%, or 493.75 points, to 25,030.35. The Sensex gained 2.17% to 81,028.02. That's a seventh straight gain.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Foreign investors bought a record 45,960 crore rupees of Indian shares over the week. The Nifty gained about 8.6% in that week.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: And Sunday's Muhurat session?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Almost flat. The Nifty slipped 6.65 points to 25,023.70, and the Sensex 28.62 points to 80,999.40. It was the first red Muhurat close since 2017.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Who moved the market?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Banks led. ICICI Bank rose 4.75% and HDFC Bank 3.72%. M&M was the Nifty's top gainer.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Seven days up, about 8.6% in a week. Isn't this just a rally running on borrowed time?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Now, why it matters. This rally rests on foreign money. Monday tests whether that buying continues into a new Samvat year, with US inflation data on Tuesday.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: What should I watch?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Whether the Nifty holds above 25,000 and foreign buying continues in Monday's provisional data. A fall back below 24,900 would signal foreign selling has returned.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Stocks in focus: HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Reliance. Sentiment: positive.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Rapid fire. Story two: banks are carrying the whole market.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Nifty Bank rose 2.27% to 59,086 on Friday, an eight-month high. Nifty Financial Services gained 2.57%.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: In Sunday's Muhurat session, Nifty Bank slipped 0.27%.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: banks carry the largest weight in foreign buying, so they decide the index's next move. Sentiment: positive. Stocks in focus: ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank, SBI, Kotak Bank.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story three: Tata Steel beats, and a broker turns bullish.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Profit attributable to owners rose 18.2% to 3,666 crore rupees. Standalone EBITDA of 10,320 crore rupees beat Nuvama's estimate of 9,900 crore.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Nuvama upgraded the stock on Sunday, and it rose about 2.1% to around 190 rupees in the Muhurat session.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: So what's still the problem?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Europe. India margins are strong, but the UK business remains the drag.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: Indian steel margins are holding up well. Sentiment: positive. Stocks in focus: Tata Steel, JSW Steel, Jindal Steel, SAIL.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story four: Hindalco's profit jumps 59%.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Profit rose 59% to 7,532 crore rupees, on revenue up 39% to 91,708 crore. Nuvama also upgraded Hindalco.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: India EBITDA, including Utkal Alumina, came in at 8,450 crore rupees, against Nuvama's 7,080 crore estimate.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Didn't the market already react on Friday?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Barely. Friday's close of 958.40 rupees came only an hour after results. Monday is the first full session to price the beat.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: strong aluminium volumes help India's metals story. Sentiment: positive. Stocks in focus: Hindalco, Nalco, Vedanta, Hindustan Zinc.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story five: the rupee has its best day in weeks.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The rupee rose 52 paise to 93.89 per dollar on Friday, from 94.41. Foreign investors bought 13,750 crore rupees of shares that day.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Can it keep going?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The dollar index rose about 0.7% after strong US payrolls, which pulls against the rupee on Monday.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: a firmer rupee lowers India's import bill. Sentiment: mixed. Stocks in focus: Infosys, TCS, BPCL.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story six: oil eases, but stays near 98 dollars.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Brent fell 0.64% to 97.67 dollars a barrel on Monday. WTI slipped 0.40% to 90.51 dollars.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Donald Trump told CNN fresh strikes on Iran were highly unlikely to be needed if it signs a strong agreement.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Then why isn't oil falling harder?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Both the US and Iran reported vessels hit near the Strait of Hormuz.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: oil near 98 dollars is still India's biggest macro cost. Sentiment: mixed. Stocks in focus: BPCL, IOC, HPCL, IndiGo.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story seven: US jobs came in hot. Why should I care?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: US employers added 165,000 jobs in October, against about 59,000 expected. Unemployment fell to 4.1%, from 4.2%.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The 10-year Treasury yield rose 2 basis points to 4.86%. Markets see roughly 78% odds of a December Fed hike.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: US yields set the pull on foreign money into India, and Tuesday's CPI is the next test. Sentiment: negative.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story eight: IT is sitting out the rally.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Nifty IT rose only 0.43% on Friday, while the Nifty gained 2.01%. Infosys rose 1.20% to 1,181.40 rupees.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Infosys was then among the Sensex's biggest losers in the Muhurat session, even after the Nasdaq rose 1.09%.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: IT is funding the rotation into banks. Sentiment: negative. Stocks in focus: Infosys, TCS, HCLTech, Wipro.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story nine: Titan hits 5,000 rupees on Dhanteras.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Titan rose 3.42% to 5,000 rupees on Friday, and is up about 10% in three sessions after a 54% profit rise.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Jewellery start-up GIVA raised 975 crore rupees over the weekend. Kalyan Jewellers reports on Tuesday.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: with the festival catalyst past, this tests post-Diwali jewellery demand. Sentiment: mixed. Stocks in focus: Titan, Kalyan Jewellers, Senco Gold.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Last one. Story ten: M&M keeps climbing.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: M&M rose 5.11% to 3,287.20 rupees on Friday, after a 6.5% jump on Thursday. That's about 11% in two sessions.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Any sign it's cooling?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Yes. It was the Sensex's biggest loser in Sunday's Muhurat session, the first sign of profit-taking.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: M&M is the auto bellwether this results season. Sentiment: mixed. Stocks in focus: M&M, Maruti, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: What to watch today: foreign flows, whether the Nifty holds 25,000, and US CPI on Tuesday.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: That's Ripple Daily. Full stories and sources are in the show notes. This is news, not investment advice. We're not SEBI-registered advisers.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: See you tomorrow morning.
